column1: 1:1|The word of the LORD came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.|Retains all four ancestral generations and the exact royal setting.
1:2|“I will sweep everything away\nfrom the face of the ground,” declares the LORD.|Preserves the sweeping totality and ground image.

1:3|“I will sweep away humans and animals;
I will sweep away the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea,
the stumbling blocks along with the wicked.
I will cut humanity off from the face of the ground,”
declares the LORD.|Retains all creature categories and the difficult stumbling-blocks phrase without deleting it.

1:4|“I will stretch out my hand against Judah
and everyone who lives in Jerusalem.
From this place I will cut off what remains of Baal,
the name of the idol-priests along with the priests,|Keeps the two priest terms distinguishable and the continuing list open.

1:5|those who bow on the rooftops to heaven’s army,\nthose who bow and swear allegiance to the LORD\nwhile also swearing by their king,|Follows the pointed their-king reading and notes the Milcom alternative.
1:6|those who turn away from following the LORD,\nwho neither seek the LORD nor inquire of him.”|Preserves both repeated divine names and the paired failures to seek.

1:7|Be silent before the Lord GOD,
for the day of the LORD is near!
The LORD has prepared a sacrifice
and consecrated his invited guests.|Retains the unsettling sacrifice/guest image without assigning each participant.

1:8|“On the day of the LORD’s sacrifice\nI will punish the officials, the king’s sons,\nand everyone dressed in foreign clothing.|Keeps royal sons and clothing as stated rather than interpreting their precise offense.
1:9|On that day I will punish everyone who leaps over the threshold,\nwho fills their master’s house with violence and deceit.|Retains the obscure threshold practice, with context left to a note.

1:10|On that day,” declares the LORD,
“a cry will rise from the Fish Gate,
a wail from the Second Quarter,
and a great crash from the hills.|Preserves Jerusalem locations and the sequence of sounds.

1:11|Wail, you who live in the Mortar!\nAll the merchant people are silenced;\nall who weigh out silver are cut off.|Chooses merchant for Canaan in the trade context and preserves the district’s literal name.

1:12|At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps
and punish the men settled on their dregs,
who say in their hearts,
‘The LORD will do neither good nor harm.’|Keeps the wine-dregs image and the complacent claim in direct speech.

1:13|Their wealth will become plunder,
their houses a desolation.
They will build houses but not live in them,
plant vineyards but not drink their wine.”|Retains paired frustrated actions and concrete losses.

1:14|The great day of the LORD is near—
near and coming very quickly!
Listen to the day of the LORD:
there the warrior cries out bitterly.|Keeps near repeated and the sudden auditory summons.

1:15|That day is a day of fury,
a day of distress and anguish,
a day of ruin and devastation,
a day of darkness and gloom,
a day of clouds and thick darkness,|Retains the anaphoric day-of structure and paired terms.
1:16|a day of horn blast and battle cry\nagainst fortified cities\nand their high corner towers.|Completes the preceding day list and identifies the defensive corners naturally.

1:17|“I will bring distress upon humanity,
and they will walk like the blind,
because they have sinned against the LORD.
Their blood will be poured out like dust,
their flesh like dung.”|Preserves the violent bodily images and the stated causal connection.

1:18|Neither their silver nor their gold can rescue them
on the day of the LORD’s fury.
The whole earth will be consumed
by the fire of his jealousy,
for he will make a sudden, complete end
of everyone who lives on the earth.|Keeps universal scope, jealousy, and the suddenness rather than reducing the warning to wealth alone.
2:1|Gather yourselves; gather together,\nunwanted nation,|Retains the repeated gathering call and chooses unwanted for the difficult participle, with alternative noted.

2:2|before the decree gives birth,
before the day passes like chaff,
before the LORD’s burning anger comes upon you,
before the day of the LORD’s anger comes upon you.|Keeps the birthing decree and chaff images alongside the repeated before clauses.

2:3|Seek the LORD, all you humble people of the earth
who carry out his judgment.
Seek righteousness; seek humility.
Perhaps you will be hidden
on the day of the LORD’s anger.|Preserves all three seek commands and the consequential perhaps.

2:4|For Gaza will be abandoned,
Ashkelon left desolate.
Ashdod will be driven out at noon,
and Ekron uprooted.|Retains each city, noon, and the uprooting verb that echoes its name.

2:5|Woe to those who live along the coast,
the nation of the Cherethites!
The word of the LORD is against you,
Canaan, land of the Philistines:
“I will destroy you until no inhabitant remains.”|Distinguishes the coast’s named people from the quoted threat.
2:6|The coast will become pastureland,\nshepherds’ shelters and pens for flocks.|Chooses shelters for the uncertain middle noun without inventing a geographic detail.

2:7|The coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah.
There they will graze,
and in Ashkelon’s houses they will lie down at evening,
for the LORD their God will attend to them
and restore their fortunes.|Retains shepherding imagery for the remnant and the restoration idiom.

2:8|“I have heard Moab’s taunts
and the insults of the Ammonites,
who taunted my people
and boasted against their territory.|Preserves the territorial aspect and repeated taunting.

2:9|So, as I live,” declares the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel,
“Moab will become like Sodom
and the Ammonites like Gomorrah—
a tangle of nettles, a salt pit, a lasting wasteland.
The remnant of my people will plunder them;
those left of my nation will possess them.”|Keeps the oath, both comparisons, and the read my-nation form.
2:10|This is what they will receive for their pride,\nbecause they taunted and boasted\nagainst the people of the LORD of Armies.|Connects judgment to the repeated proud taunts without adding motive.

2:11|The LORD will be fearsome against them,
for he will starve all the gods of the earth.
All the coastlands of the nations will bow to him,
each from its own place.|Retains the striking starving-gods image and geographically dispersed worship.
2:12|“You Cushites too—\nthey will be slain by my sword.”|Preserves the abrupt you/they shift instead of treating it as an unnoticed grammatical error.

2:13|He will stretch his hand northward
and destroy Assyria.
He will make Nineveh a wasteland,
dry as the wilderness.|Keeps both named imperial locations and the dry-wilderness comparison.

2:14|Herds will lie down within her,
creatures of every kind.
The desert owl and the hedgehog
will lodge on her capitals.
A voice will sing in the window;
ruin will lie on the threshold,
for her cedarwork is laid bare.|Retains architectural ruins and provisional animal identifications with uncertainty noted.

2:15|This is the carefree city that lived secure,
saying in her heart, “I am, and no one else!”
How she has become a wasteland,
a resting place for wild animals!
Everyone who passes hisses and waves a hand.|Keeps the city’s exclusive boast and the scornful gestures.
3:1|Woe to the rebellious, polluted city,\nthe city that oppresses!|Preserves the threefold indictment before the city is named later.

3:2|She has not listened to a voice
or accepted correction.
She has not trusted the LORD
or drawn near to her God.|Retains the four negatives and relational progression.
3:3|Her officials within her are roaring lions;\nher judges are wolves at dusk,\nleaving nothing to gnaw by morning.|Keeps the paired predatory offices and the evening/morning contrast.
3:4|Her prophets are reckless, treacherous men;\nher priests profane what is holy\nand do violence to instruction.|Preserves specific male prophets and the violence verb applied to instruction.

3:6|“I have cut off nations;
their corner towers are deserted.
I have laid waste their streets, with no one passing through.
Their cities are destroyed, without a person,
without an inhabitant.|Keeps the repeated absence of inhabitants and the city imagery.

3:7|I said, ‘Surely you will fear me
and accept correction.’
Then her dwelling would not be cut off,
whatever I had appointed against her.
But they rose early to corrupt all their deeds.|Preserves the difficult you/her/they shifts and the deliberate eagerness to corrupt.

3:8|So wait for me,” declares the LORD,
“for the day I rise to seize prey.
For my decision is to gather nations,
to assemble kingdoms,
to pour my indignation on them,
all my burning anger.
The whole earth will be consumed
by the fire of my jealousy.|Follows pointed prey while noting witness alternative and repeats the fire-of-jealousy phrase.
3:9|Then I will give the peoples purified lips,\nso they may all call on the name of the LORD\nand serve him shoulder to shoulder.|Keeps lips and shared-shoulder images in idiomatic English.
3:10|From beyond the rivers of Cush,\nmy worshipers, my scattered people,\nwill bring my offering.|Treats the difficult daughter-of-my-dispersed phrase collectively with its uncertainty noted.

3:11|On that day you will no longer be ashamed
of all the deeds by which you rebelled against me.
For then I will remove from your midst
those who revel in your pride;
you will no longer be arrogant on my holy mountain.|Preserves both the removal of proud people and the changed community.
3:12|I will leave among you a people poor and lowly,\nand they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.|Retains material poverty as well as lowliness rather than spiritualizing both terms.

3:13|The remnant of Israel will do no injustice
and speak no lies;
no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths.
They will graze and lie down,
with no one to terrify them.”|Preserves ethical parallels and the peaceful flock image.

3:14|Sing out, daughter Zion!
Raise a shout, Israel!
Rejoice and celebrate with all your heart,
daughter Jerusalem!|Keeps the feminine city personification and distinct calls to joy.

3:15|The LORD has removed the judgments against you
and cleared your enemy away.
The king of Israel, the LORD, is among you;
you will no longer fear harm.|Retains both LORD repetitions and the king designation.
3:16|On that day Jerusalem will be told:\n“Do not be afraid, Zion;\ndo not let your hands fall limp.|Keeps the bodily discouragement image in direct encouragement.

3:18|“I will gather those grieving over the appointed festival;\nthey were from you,\na burden of reproach upon her.|Marks the return to first-person divine speech, retaining the difficult clause and pronoun change with an explicit note.

3:19|Look, at that time I will deal with all who oppress you.
I will save the lame and gather the outcast.
I will give them praise and renown
in every land where they were shamed.|Preserves the vulnerable groups and the reversal of shame, noting the compressed last clause.

3:20|At that time I will bring you in,
at the time I gather you.
I will give you renown and praise
among all the peoples of the earth
when I restore your fortunes before your eyes,”
says the LORD.|Keeps repeated time/gathering and the witnessed restoration.
